items.justification: Update activation and recovery is unrelated to monitoring internal model states.
Communications cryptography and staff threat awareness are unrelated obligations.
A concerns the device's model designation label; B concerns notice of AI model updates. The shared word "model" denotes different things.
Both require security-relevant information to be documented for those operating the product; A as user guidance, B as system documentation content.
Distributing updates and verifying them on receipt are distinct obligations on different parties in one update chain.
Validating inbound input and preventing information leakage through outputs do not combine into a single nameable control.
Guidance on checking secure state is unrelated to asset disposal at transfer of ownership.
Monitoring one's own product for vulnerabilities and risk-assessing adopted external components are distinct parts of one risk management duty.
Transport cryptography and least-privilege permissions between systems are unrelated controls.
Key uniqueness is unrelated to the up-front business case and risk documentation.
Input validation and due diligence on external components pursue different objectives.
Input validation is a technical control; documentation content is a disclosure duty.
Shipping the fix promptly and giving users notice before it lands are distinct duties in one update process.
Input validation and asset tracking processes share no objective.
Both pursue identification and management of security risks to one's own systems; A reactively through vulnerability monitoring, B proactively through threat modelling.
Both keep credentials and sensitive assets out of reach in the codebase; A by prohibiting hard-coded parameters, B by requiring processes and tools that secure assets.
Documenting sensing capabilities is unrelated to due diligence on an external provider.
Device model labelling and justification for using undocumented components share no objective.
Recording residual risk decisions and continuously reviewing against risk appetite are distinct steps of one risk management process.
Key lifecycle management and superfluous model functionality are unrelated risks.
Both govern sensitive material at end of life; A covers the entire lifecycle of security parameters, B the deletion of data and configuration at decommissioning.
Continuous vulnerability monitoring and re-testing after a major version change are distinct assurance activities over a product's life.
Both minimize unnecessary capability; A restricts software privileges to the least needed, B requires the risk of superfluous model functionality to be managed.
Key uniqueness is unrelated to monitoring model behaviour drift.
Both require controls proportionate to risk and sensitivity; A for the cryptography used, B for the system's usage relative to its training data.
Both require accessible user-facing information about the product; A the support period, B its limitations and failure modes.
Debug interface protection is unrelated to communicating unresolved threats.
A detects unauthorized change; B assesses risk arising from authorized configuration change. Different objectives.
Using evaluated implementations is unrelated to asset disposal at transfer.
Key uniqueness and post-incident user support share no objective.
Update activation and recovery is unrelated to logging configuration and prompt changes.
Key uniqueness is unrelated to verifying that specified controls were implemented.
B's audit trail names incident response as what it supports, which is the process A requires be documented and completed in bounded time.
Both prevent a user from gaining unintended influence over system behaviour through the interface; A by validating input, B by evaluating output.
Both concern notifying users about updates; A the user's control over receiving notifications, B the duty to notify before updating.
Publishing a disclosure policy and conveying data handling practices are different disclosures with different objectives.
Using evaluated cryptographic implementations differs from publishing hashes for downstream verification.
Restricting the product technically to its intended use and telling users which uses are prohibited are the technical and informational halves of scope enforcement.
Tamper resistance of a device identity is unrelated to permission scoping between systems.
Publishing a support period differs from providing operators preview access to evaluate model changes.
